# docs_audit_report — 2026-06-28

## TL;DR (stranger's 30-second take)
The hero is genuinely strong — one clear sentence, a `pip install`, and a
concrete 47+28 example buy enough goodwill to keep scrolling. But a careful
evaluator bounces at two places: the page can't tell me its own license (MIT-0
in the badge, Apache 2.0 in the footer), and the "Evidence" section — the part
that's supposed to earn trust — is a wall of unexplained acronyms with a FoVer
number that contradicts the hero. Net: intrigued, then distrustful.

## TOP 3 PROBLEMS
1. License contradiction — hero badge + `<meta>` say "MIT-0", footer says
   "Apache 2.0 License". A stranger literally cannot tell what license this is.
2. "What we measured" (Results) is an insider acronym wall (SVAMP, CRANE,
   VeriCoT, HalluGuard v3, PRM-BiasBench, CCTU, "k=5 ensemble", "0.0pp") AND
   contradicts the headline: hero says "FoVer 0.9131", a result card says
   "0.125 FoVer baseline".
3. Internal research-loop narrative leaks everywhere — "382 Completed
   milestones" as a vanity stat, a "Research operations" capability card,
   "operator-initiated upload", "paper-v6", "Repinned from v2 0.9857". Reads
   like an internal status dashboard, not a product page.

## DETAILED FINDINGS

### Bloat
- Nav bar (lines 264–285) — 12 text links + 2 buttons = 14 clickable items —
  cap ~6–7. A stranger has no idea which to click; Problem/Capabilities/
  Results/Quick Start/Report/Paper/Writing/Roadmap is an internal TOC, not
  top-level navigation.
- "Recent progress" r-card (line 312) — ~60 words AND four distinct claims
  (PyPI, HF mirror, two AUROCs, repin history, canonical repo) crammed into
  one card — cap 60 words / one idea. The repin/v2 history belongs in the blog
  post it already links, not the hero.
- Whole page is card-heavy: 7 capability cards + 12 result cards + 7 blog
  cards = 26 cards in grids. Individually under caps, but collectively a
  stranger skims none. Consider cutting Results to ~6 headline rows.

### Internal jargon
- Stats bar (line 306) — "382 Completed milestones" — "milestone" is an
  internal research-loop unit; means nothing to an outsider and isn't a
  product virtue.
- Recent-progress card (line 312) — "5-seed dual-condition", "architecture-only
  0.8947", "Repinned from v2 0.9857" — insider methodology shorthand.
- Results cards (lines 549, 554, 559, 564, 569, 574) — "SVAMP", "EstimationVerifier",
  "CRANE", "VeriCoT", "PRM-BiasBench-style", "HalluGuard v3", "CCTU",
  "k=5 ensemble", "Ising-guided fuzzing", "0.0pp", "TP rate" — none defined.
  A stranger cannot evaluate a single one of these claims.
- Safety card (line 530) — "(publication gate)" — internal process label.
- "Research operations" card (lines 469–477) — "adversarial-verify pass",
  "methodology-incomplete artifacts", "headline claims" — describes how the
  project polices itself, not anything the user can check.
- TTC & PREM card (lines 497–499) — "Process-Reward Energy Model (PREM)
  variance… intrinsic motivation for continuous self-learning" — the single
  most opaque card on the page; pure jargon with a vague benefit.
- Preprint (lines 584, 594) — "paper-v6", "operator-initiated upload",
  "non-operator environment" — "operator" is undefined project-speak.

### Per-milestone narrative
- The page mostly avoids ".NNN" milestone refs (good), but the *flavor*
  persists: "382 Completed milestones" (line 306), "Repinned from v2 0.9857
  after pre-submission adversarial audit" (line 312), and the entire "Research
  operations" card (lines 469–477) read like retrospective/status copy rather
  than landing-page value props.

### Inconsistencies
- License: "MIT-0" (line 7 meta, line 291 badge) vs "Apache 2.0 License"
  (line 766 footer). Direct contradiction.
- FoVer AUROC: "0.9131 … FoVer" headline (lines 308, 312, 589) vs "0.125 FoVer
  baseline" (line 550). Same name, wildly different numbers, no disambiguation
  — looks self-contradictory even if technically different artifacts.
- The 47+28 example uses "= 76" in the intro and "Whole-answer check" card
  (lines 329, 343) but "= 7" in the "One-word-at-a-time" card (line 338).
  Reading as a typo to a stranger; the mid-generation intent isn't obvious.
- r-meter bar widths are semantically inconsistent: +3.0 pts → 14.6% width,
  +4.9 pts → 66.7% width, while absolute scores map 1:1 (0.91 → 91%). The bars
  encode nothing consistent and quietly mislead.

### Missing essentials
- Clear license — contradicted (above). This is the one fact an adopter needs
  and the page fails it.
- Who maintains it — only "© Ian Blenke" in the footer; no one-line "who/what
  is this team" anywhere. Fine-ish for OSS, but combined with the autonomous-
  loop framing a stranger may wonder if anything here is human-reviewed.
- Trust anchor present and good (independent CI reproduction, line 589–593) —
  but it's buried in the Preprint section, not near the headline 0.9131 stat
  where the skeptic first sees the number.

### Fabrication signals
- "GSM8K extraction TP rate: 0.5 → 1.0" (line 560) — a perfect 1.0 with no
  sample size or CI.
- "k=5 ensemble catches 60/60 attacks" (line 565) — 100% on N=60, no anchor.
- "2.0× speedup, identical losses" (line 540) — "identical" reads as
  suspiciously exact.
- "0.0pp accuracy delta with 4.4% cost savings" (line 570) — a result card
  whose headline achievement is "changed nothing"; weak and odd to feature.
- "99.3% of wrong code flagged" (line 431) — high but at least anchored to

- (Blog teaser) "Zero false positives" (line 741) — perfect claim, though it's
  a blog hook not a headline.

### Structural / rendering bugs (a stranger sees broken layout, not copy)
- Stats bar (lines 304–315): an `.r-card` is nested *inside* `.stats-bar`
  alongside the four `.stat` numbers, plus a stray extra `</div>` at line 314.
  A prose result card jammed into the headline-number row will render oddly.
- Features grid: the TTC & PREM card (lines 495–501) sits *outside* the inner
  `.bento-grid` (grid closes at line 494). Likely renders detached/full-width,
  breaking the "seven capabilities" grid.
- Results section: `.results-grid` closes (line 578) but `.container` is never
  closed before `</section>` (line 579). Unbalanced DOM.
- `.num` span class is used in the Rust sample (lines 643, 652) but never
  defined in CSS (only kw/fn/str/cm exist, line 231) — numbers render
  uncolored; dead markup.

### Framing incoherence
- Section header "What you can check" / "Seven capabilities" (lines 415–416),
  but 3 of the 7 cards — Research operations, APIs & portable memory, TTC &
  PREM — are not things you check. Mixing verification capabilities with
  project-meta features under one count makes the whole section read as padded.

## WHAT'S WORKING
- The hero is excellent: "Catch the reasoning errors your LLM states with total
  confidence," the plain-language sub-paragraph, `pip install carnot-ebm`, and
  the concrete 47+28 walkthrough are exactly what a stranger needs.
- "How it works" (Extract → Check → Repair) and the Python quickstart are clear,
  honest, and compelling — a reader could actually try it.
- The blog teasers are a genuine asset: candid "we caught ourselves cheating /
  retracted two claims" posts read as unusually credible and self-critical.
